title: BE-CTDE: Blockchain-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Anomaly Detection and Token Economics
abstract: arXiv:2610.34121v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning supports cooperative decision-making in Internet of Things systems, but strategic deviations can disrupt coordination and undermine confidence in the training process. This paper proposes Blockchain-Enabled Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (BE-CTDE), which uses blockchain as an active training-management layer. A behavioral verifier compares executed trajectories with shared-policy recommendations; its flags drive a token mechanism combining slashing, burning, rewards, and compensation. Retained balances determine each agent's contribution to the global policy update, connecting auditable behavior to learning influence. We derive a one-round incentive condition that accounts for action-dependent compensation and the payoff from deviation, and a finite expected exclusion-time bound under explicit conditional detection and accounting assumptions, showing perfect detection is unnecessary.

translated_title: BE-CTDE：基于区块链的具备异常检测与代币经济的多智能体强化学习
translated_abstract: 多智能体强化学习支持物联网系统中的协作决策，但策略性偏离行为可能破坏协调并削弱对训练过程的信心。本文提出区块链赋能的集中式训练与分散式执行框架（BE-CTDE），将区块链用作主动的训练管理层。行为验证器将已执行的轨迹与共享策略的建议进行比较，其标记将驱动一个结合罚没、销毁、奖励和补偿的代币机制。智能体的保留余额决定其对全局策略更新的贡献，从而将可审计的行为与学习影响力关联起来。我们推导了考虑动作相关补偿与偏离收益的单轮激励条件，并在明确的条件检测与记账假设下给出了有限的期望排除时间上界，证明完美检测并非必要。
tldr: 该论文提出BE-CTDE框架，将区块链作为主动训练管理层，通过行为验证器与结合罚没、销毁、奖励和补偿的代币机制抑制多智能体强化学习中的策略性偏离，并将智能体的代币余额与其对全局策略更新的影响力挂钩，同时证明无需完美检测即可保证激励有效与有限时间排除偏差者。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes BE-CTDE, a blockchain-enabled centralized training with decentralized execution framework that uses a behavioral verifier and a token mechanism combining slashing, burning, rewards, and compensation to deter strategic deviations in multi-agent reinforcement learning, links agents' retained balances to their influence on global policy updates, and shows that perfect detection is unnecessary via a one-round incentive condition and a finite expected exclusion-time bound.
